g.title: Malignant_Hyperthermia_QSP_Model
g.text: Malignant hyperthermia is not a fever. It is
ONE driver read through TWO stores of very different size
The driver is myoplasmic Ca²⁺; the two stores are the body's CO₂ store (60 mL·mmHg⁻¹) and the body's heat store (158 kJ·°C⁻¹). Divided by the same excess flux they give
0.15 min per mmHg of EtCO₂ and 17 min per °C of core temperature

so one degree of fever costs as much clock time as ~111 mmHg of EtCO₂, and the entire capnograph scale is exhausted before the thermometer moves. The diagnostic ordering is arithmetic, not convention.
Second axis: the volatile agent is the term that
the event; ROS-driven redox sensitisation of RyR1 is the term that

it. Removing the agent deletes only the first — which is why turning the vaporiser off was never enough, and why dantrolene (which blocks the channel whatever opens it) took mortality from ~80% to <5%.

Third axis: every non-dantrolene manoeuvre treats a READOUT. Hyperventilation normalises EtCO₂ and active cooling normalises temperature while the driver runs untouched — the model kills the patient in both arms with a normal-looking monitor.

g.title: cluster_gene
g.text: 🧬 1. Susceptibility genotype — the variant does NOT create a new pathway. It moves ONE number: the agent concentration at which RyR1 opens. Everyone has the machinery; MHS patients have a lower threshold

g.title: cluster_trig
g.text: 💨 2. Triggering agents — MAC is a CNS potency scale. RyR1 does not read MAC, it reads molar concentration, and 1 MAC spans 0.75% → 6.0% vol. That 8-fold spread is why onset time is agent-specific

g.title: cluster_pk
g.text: ⚗️ 3. Volatile PK — five gas-equivalent compartments. The muscle time constant (~2 h) is why MH onset is delayed and variable; the CIRCUIT time constant is why 'turn the vaporiser off' is not the same as 'remove the agent'

g.title: cluster_ca
g.text: 🧪 5. Ca²⁺ handling — a non-obvious result: at steady state SR release and SERCA uptake CANCEL, so the sustained myoplasmic Ca²⁺ level is set by the SARCOLEMMAL balance (SOCE in vs PMCA/NCX out). MH's plateau is an EXTRACELLULAR Ca²⁺ entry disease

g.title: cluster_redox
g.text: 🔥 6. THE SUSTAINING TERM — ROS/RNS oxidation of RyR1. This is the whole answer to 'why wasn't turning the vaporiser off enough?'. The agent starts the event; oxidised RyR1 keeps it running for hours afterwards

g.title: cluster_ryr
g.text: 🔓 4. THE SWITCH — RyR1 open probability. Hill coefficient 3.6 makes this a THRESHOLD, not a gradient: below it nothing happens at all, above it the event is committed

g.title: cluster_energy
g.text: ⚡ 7. Contraction and energetics — note that MH rigidity arises DOWNSTREAM of the neuromuscular junction, which is exactly why non-depolarising blockers cannot relieve it. When ATP runs out the rigidity becomes rigor, which is even less reversible

g.title: cluster_perf
g.text: 🩸 8. Perfusion and O₂ delivery — two OPPOSING effects of the same contracture: metabolic hyperaemia opens the bed (×5) while mechanical compression closes it (−40%). Their product sets the aerobic ceiling

g.title: cluster_co2
g.text: 📈 9. READOUT 1 (FAST) — CO₂. Store 60 mL·mmHg⁻¹ against an excess flux of ~390 mL/min ⇒ 0.15 min per mmHg. This, and nothing else, is why capnography is the first alarm

g.title: cluster_heat
g.text: 🌡️ 10. READOUT 2 (SLOW) — heat. Core store 158 kJ·°C⁻¹ against an excess of ~155 W ⇒ 17 min per °C. The word 'hyperthermia' names the LAST thing that happens

g.title: cluster_acid
g.text: 🧯 11. Acid-base — MH is the classic MIXED acidosis, and the mixture is informative: the respiratory half tracks the CO₂ store, the metabolic half tracks the O₂ debt

g.title: cluster_injury
g.text: 💥 12. Rhabdomyolysis — FOUR multiplicative drivers. Because they multiply, dropping any one of them (Ca²⁺, heat, ATP) buys more than its arithmetic share

g.title: cluster_complic
g.text: 🚨 13. Systemic complications — Larach's four registry outcomes (cardiac, renal, DIC, death). Note that the two fastest killers, hyperkalaemic arrest and DIC, are driven by DIFFERENT variables (K⁺ vs thermal dose)

g.title: cluster_rx
g.text: 💊 14. Therapy — exactly ONE agent acts on the driver. Everything else in this cluster acts on a readout or a consequence. The model's treatment arms make that distinction quantitative

g.title: cluster_dx
g.text: 🔬 15. Diagnosis — the contracture test measures exactly the parameter the genotype moves (EC50), which is why a functional assay still outperforms sequencing

g.title: cluster_ddx
g.text: 🧭 16. Differential — every one of these raises EtCO₂ and/or temperature. The discriminator the model exposes: in MH the EtCO₂ rise is REFRACTORY to increased minute ventilation, because the source term, not the elimination term, has changed

g.title: cluster_out
g.text: 🎯 17. Endpoints — the model's own treatment arms (MHS_high, sevoflurane 2% + succinylcholine, first sign at 45 min). Read the 'monitor' column against the 'outcome' column

g.title: E_nmba
g.text: ★ Rocuronium / vecuronium act at the nAChR —
UPSTREAM of RyR1. In this model they have
EXACTLY ZERO effect on MH rigidity.
Masseter spasm that persists after full
blockade is therefore diagnostic, not paradoxical

(and of MH first presenting as an arrest

a normal myoglobin at 12 h excludes nothing)

g.title: I_k

g.title: D_dose
g.text: ★ Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV, repeat q5-10 min
to ≥10 mg/kg (30 mg/kg has been used)

g.title: D_prep
g.text: ★ Dantrium/Revonto: 20 mg per vial in 60 mL
sterile water — 9 vials, 540 mL, ~18 min of shaking
is an input DELAY, and delay is the outcome variable
